title: MAX98357A I²S amplifier
_note: 7 header pins in one row, from the Adafruit board file. OUT− and OUT+ are the 3.5 mm screw terminal on the far edge, about 13 mm from the header, with − on the LRC side and + on the Vin side. terminal: the pin is on top of the module, not in a breadboard hole; the speaker leads or a wire go into it. row and col give its place over the bench. The header is one row, so the part stays on one side of the center gap.

datasheet.summary: A class-D amplifier. It reads I²S data from the board and drives a small speaker.

pins.LRC: Left/right clock (word select). The board tells the amplifier when each sample starts.
pins.BCLK: Bit clock. The board sets the speed of the data.
pins.DIN: Data in. The sound samples go from the board to the amplifier on this pin.
pins.GAIN: Gain select. Leave it open for 9 dB. Connect it to ground for 12 dB (louder), or to Vin for 6 dB (quieter).
pins.SD: Shutdown and channel select. Connect it to ground to turn the amplifier off. On this breakout, a resistor pulls SD up: left open, it plays left and right mixed. (On the bare chip, SD must be driven high.)
pins.GND: Ground. Connect it to the ground of the board.
pins.OUT-: Speaker output, minus. Connect it only to the speaker, never to ground.
pins.OUT+: Speaker output, plus. Connect it only to the speaker, never to ground.
